extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants and practitioners (patent attorneys/agents, in-house counsel, IP managers) evaluating expedited examination options
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on selecting between the Patent Prosecution Highway (PPH) and the USPTO Track One prioritized examination program to accelerate patent prosecution, covering eligibility, process, fees, and filing tips for U.S. filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: PPH (Patent Prosecution Highway) — overview
rubrics_metrics.description: The Patent Prosecution Highway (PPH) accelerates examination of corresponding patent applications filed in participating IP offices. If at least one claim is found allowable by a first office, the applicant can request fast-track examination in a second office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: By leveraging existing expedited procedures, PPH enables quicker and more efficient patent decisions—at no additional cost. PPH is useful when there is at least one allowed claim in an Office of Earlier Examination (OEE) that can be used to request accelerated examination in the U.S. or another participating office.

rubrics_metrics.name: U.S. PPH eligibility requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: U.S. patent applications eligible for PPH must meet the following requirements: At least one claim in a corresponding application must be allowed at an eligible* Office of Earlier Examination (OEE). The U.S. application must have the same earliest priority date as the OEE application. Substantive examination of the U.S. application must not have started.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quick Tips for Filing a U.S. PPH Request: Notify Legal Counsel Early — File after at least one claim is allowed in an OEE and before U.S. examination begins. Submit OEE Work Product — Include the latest document showing allowed claim(s); provide an English translation if needed (machine/manual accepted). Share Allowed OEE Claims in English — Helps prepare the claim correspondence table for the PPH request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Track One (Prioritized Examination) — overview
rubrics_metrics.description: Track One is the USPTO’s prioritized examination program for utility and plant patent applications, offering a final decision within 12 months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track One provides special status with fewer requirements than accelerated examination and no need for a pre-examination search. It is available for a fee and may be requested with the original filing or with a Request for Continued Examination (RCE). Use Track One when speed to a final decision (within 12 months) is a primary objective and fee-based prioritized processing is acceptable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Track One eligibility and filing requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Application must include a specification with no multiple-dependent claims, max 4 independent claims, and no more than 30 total claims. Include any required drawings. Must be filed via USPTO’s electronic filing system (EFS-Web or Patent Center).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These claim-count and formatting limits are preconditions for Track One prioritized examination; applications exceeding the limits may incur fees or be ineligible. Ensure required drawings are included and file through USPTO's accepted electronic systems to satisfy procedural requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Track One fees and applicable additional fees
rubrics_metrics.description: The fees required to be paid on a utility patent application upon filing a request for prioritized examination of that application are: Basic filing fee, Search fee, Examination fee, Publication fee, Prioritized examination processing fee, Prioritized examination fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article lists the applicable statutory/regulatory fee citations (e.g., 37 CFR 1.16(a) basic filing fee; 1.16(k) search fee; 1.16(o) examination fee; 1.18(d) publication fee; 1.17(i) processing fee; 1.17(c) prioritized examination fee). Additional applicable fees may include: application size fee (37 CFR 1.16(s)) if specification and drawings exceed 100 sheets; excess independent claim fee (37 CFR 1.16(h)) if independent claims exceed three; excess claim fee (37 CFR 1.16(i)) if total claims exceed twenty; and, if requesting prioritized examination for an RCE, the RCE fee (37 CFR 1.17(e)). Confirm current fee amounts and rule citations on the USPTO fee schedule before filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparative tradeoffs when choosing between PPH and Track One
rubrics_metrics.description: While both aim to accelerate examination, they differ in eligibility, cost, and process: PPH speeds up patent examination by using fast-track procedures across participating offices at no extra fee; Track One offers prioritized examination within 12 months for a fee, with fewer requirements than accelerated examination and no pre-examination search.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider eligibility (do you have an allowed claim in an OEE?), cost (PPH generally has no extra fee; Track One requires multiple fees), timing (Track One targets a final decision within 12 months), and prosecution strategy. The article cautions that Track One may pressure examiners to limit claims or reject applications quickly, whereas PPH leverages the examiner’s prior knowledge/allowance to support smoother prosecution. Choose based on whether fee-based speed or leveraging prior allowance and potentially smoother prosecution better fits your objectives.
